title: Strategic Account Admission Protocol and Roadmap Velocity Hedging
creator: Maya Patel
description: Goal: Define and implement a repeatable admission protocol for strategic (top) accounts that converts signals into a quantified commitment and a dynamic roadmap velocity hedge. We need a single source of truth that: 1) admits or deprioritizes incoming top-account asks, 2) quantifies probability and expected effort against roadmap velocity, and 3) produces deterministic output for Exec/CS/Sales (OKR-aligned commitments or deferrals).
background: We frequently receive high-touch escalation requests from strategic customers that bypass standard intake. Current ad-hoc decisions create scope churn, missed SLAs for other customers, and unpredictable roadmap velocity. Existing artifacts (customer intake playbooks) are fragmented across Confluence and PMs' inboxes. This initiative standardizes admission criteria with a numerical hedging model so product trade-offs are transparent and auditable.
acceptance_criteria: Admission flow defined: signal taxonomy, minimum evidence, and acceptance gates documented in Confluence
Quantified intake score implemented (0-100) with documented mapping to roadmap lanes (FastTrack / Evaluate / Backlog / Decline)
Velocity hedge model prototype: shows projected Q2 impact on roadmap capacity for 3 sample requests
Console view created in Redwood Console: per-account intake record with decision rationale visible to Exec/CS/Eng
Escalation SLA: admission decision (accept/deflect) within 10 business days for high-sensitivity accounts
Stakeholder sign-off from Sales leadership, CS leadership, and VP Product
proposed_approach: Phase 1: Design & criteria (2 weeks) — interview 8 high-touch accounts, define signal weights (strategic-fit, ARR, regulatory need, compliance risk, time-sensitivity). Phase 2: Prototype scoring engine and a lightweight Console card (1 sprint) — show score and recommended lane. Phase 3: Pilot with 3 active accounts, gather feedback, iterate on score mapping. Phase 4: Automate routing and reporting (release).
key_tradeoffs_and_risks: Tradeoff: Strict numerical thresholds increase predictability but may feel inflexible for Sales — mitigation: explicit override workflow with audit and compensation (timeboxed delivery or credit)
Risk: Over-indexing on ARR skews against strategic smaller accounts with regulatory needs — mitigation: include 'regulatory urgency' tier as a multiplier
Operational risk: extra gating could slow down genuine high-priority fixes — mitigation: 10-day SLA and emergency bypass for operational outages with CTO approval
decision_log: 2026-02-12: Decided to prioritize a numerical score over freeform triage to make cross-functional trade-offs auditable (agreed by VP Product and CS)
2026-02-18: Rejected a pure ARR-only model after interviewing 5 customers; added regulatory & integration-complexity signals
2026-02-25: Agreed to pilot Console card vs email-based intake for 6 weeks before full automation
implementation_notes: Backend: small scoring microservice (ENG-3421) to compute intake score; include deterministic inputs and timestamped rationale
Console: new UI card that surfaces score, weight breakdown, and recommended lane (design comps in Drive)
Analytics: expose cohort-level dashboards for accepted/deflected decisions and downstream impact on unit economics
Rollout: pilot to be limited to Sales accounts flagged as 'Strategic' in CRM; CS will own case reviews during pilot
metrics_and_reporting: Primary: % of top-account asks with decision within SLA (target 95% at 10 days)
Secondary: Change in roadmap churn (measured as % reprioritized commits per quarter), pipeline signal-to-commit conversion rate, NPS delta for pilot accounts
Experiment: simulate velocity hedge across Q2 (baseline vs with-admission) and report projected delta in dev points
rollout_plan: Week 1-2: finalize scoring taxonomy and thresholds; collect stakeholder sign-offs
Week 3: deliver scoring microservice + Console card prototype; UX validation with CS
Week 4-8: pilot with 3-5 strategic accounts, weekly sync with Sales/CS; log lessons
Week 9-10: iterate and prepare automated routing + reporting for broader release
